### Diagnostics summary

.large[
Before fitting a model:

* Check empirical logit plots; make transformations as needed
* Investigate any unusual observations
* Check for multicollinearity with scatterplots / correlations between quantitative explanatory variables; if needed, choose a subset of variables or combine variables

After fitting a model:

* Check quantile residual plots
* Check for multicollinearity with VIFs
* Check for influential points with Cook's distance
    * If influential points are clearly an error, can remove
    * Otherwise, report results with and without influential points
]

### Making predictions with the Titanic data

.large[
* For each passenger, we calculate $\widehat{\pi}_i$ (estimated probability of survival)
* But, we want to predict *which* passengers actually survive

.question[
How do we turn $\widehat{\pi}_i$ into a binary prediction of survival / no survival?
]
]

---

### Confusion matrix

```{r, include=F}
library(tidyverse)
titanic <- read.csv("https://sta214-s23.github.io/homework/Titanic.csv")
```

.large[
```{r, eval=F}
m1 <- glm(Survived ~ Age + Sex + as.factor(Pclass), 
          data = titanic, family = binomial)

table(Prediction = m1$fitted.values > 0.5, 
      Truth = titanic$Survived)
```

```{r, echo=F}
m1 <- glm(Survived ~ Age + Sex + as.factor(Pclass), 
          data = titanic, family = binomial)

table(Prediction = m1$fitted.values > 0.5, 
      Truth = m1$y)
```

.question[
Did we do a good job predicting survival?
]
]
